f01_se_by_question_type.message: Semantic entropy separates correct from incorrect real answers, and invented-entity questions overlap the incorrect ones

f02_option_e_by_question_type.message: The model chooses option E almost only on invented-entity questions

f03_probe_layer_sweep.message: Wrong answers become more linearly decodable between layers 12 and 18 and the curve is flat after that

f04_certification_bounds.message: With 427 certification units no threshold met the 10% target; with 3,148 units thresholds from 0.02 to 0.15 did
f04_certification_bounds.context: Clopper-Pearson bound at level 0.05/20 per threshold

f05_risk_coverage.message: All three risk scores keep the error rate under 10% up to about 40% coverage, and the frozen gate sits at 31% coverage and 5.9% error

f06_auroc_by_signal.message: The activation advantage comes from invented questions; on real questions output statistics rank errors slightly better

f07_error_direction_steering.message: Adding the layer-19 error direction does not raise the probability of E above random directions of the same norm

f08_residual_patching.message: The abstention information sits on the entity in early layers, passes through the instruction tail around layer 14 and reaches the final token from layer 15

f09_head_patching_heatmap.message: Single-head effects are confined to layers 13 to 31; L15.H4 and L17.H25 are the largest positive heads and L30.H25 is strongly negative
f09_head_patching_heatmap.context: 126 discovery pairs, final token, one head at a time

f10_circuit_size.message: Two heads are the smallest set that passes 50% restoration, so the circuit is L15.H4 and L17.H25

f11_circuit_validation.message: On held-out pairs the two-head circuit restores 51% and 21% of the gap while random head pairs restore about zero

f12_se_steering_curves.message: Circuit steering at dose 1 traces the same trade-off as the external SE wrapper over the range it covers, and random heads do nothing

f13_steering_flips.message: Steering changes wrong answers to E more often than right answers (60% vs 46%), so it is partly selective
f13_steering_flips.context: Real test questions above the SE gate, dose 1

f14_circuit_readout.message: The circuit readout separates invented from real entities almost perfectly but only weakly separates wrong from right real answers

f15_tiered_tradeoff.message: At every cost the tiered controller with the readout sits above or left of the SE wrapper, abstaining as often on unknown questions with fewer false abstentions
f15_tiered_tradeoff.context: Test role; upper left is better

f16_paired_utility_differences.message: Tiered steering with the readout improves utility at wrong-answer costs 2 and 4; at cost 1 every interval includes zero
f16_paired_utility_differences.context: Test role, 2,000 bootstrap resamples of question groups

f17_abstention_by_se_band.message: Below 0.2 nats the readout trigger catches 41% of unknown questions, where SE-based methods catch 7%
